question_type: two-hop: argmin of a monthly yield spread over a decade in a pinned issue's stacked-panel table (year labels lost in OCR), then a receipts cell for that month from an unpinned contemporaneous issue, with a millions-to-dollars conversion
decisive_step: Hop 1: anchoring the four unlabeled column groups of Table AY-1 in the pinned June 1970 issue (treasury_bulletin_1970_06.txt:4946-4984: 36 monthly rows x 4 groups, each group = three stacked years starting 1959/1962/1965/1968) so that all 120 months of 1960-1969 enter the argmin. The reference did it from the sibling issue's explicit year-label row (treasury_bulletin_1970_03.txt:4790, worklog Step 3; solution.json decisions[0]). Hop 2: reading the receipt from the 'Trust Receipts' table's 'Railroad Retirement Account' column (integer millions; treasury_bulletin_1964_04.txt:773-796, worklog Step 5) rather than the one-decimal dedicated 'Railroad Retirement Account' table or Table 1's tax-transfer line (worklog Step 7). b failed hop 1; c failed hop 2; a nearly failed hop 1 and recovered by its own check.

smallest_change.change: show_table (all modes, including --raw) and printings: when a column-group panel has no printed year (panel year0 is None, rows flagged YEAR_UNKNOWN, periods 'Y?k-MM'), anchor it automatically from a sibling printing instead of only hinting. Implementation in otables.py: after the 'N column groups share the period stub' note, call siblings() (already exists: same table id, same width, +/-1 year), pick the sibling whose corresponding group has a printed year and whose first 12 data rows of that group equal the target's cell-for-cell, adopt its year0 per group, fill periods as for a labelled table (the code path that printed '1960-11' rows for the 1970_05 sibling at c[37]), and print one NOTE line in every mode: 'NOTE: year labels missing in this printing; panels anchored from treasury_bulletin_1970_05.txt:4848 (Jan-Dec values identical): panel 1 = 1959, 1960, 1961 (rows 4949-4960, 4961-4972, 4973-4984); panel 2 = 1962, 1963, 1964; panel 3 = 1965, 1966, 1967; panel 4 = 1968, 1969, 1970 (partial). Months covered 1960-1969: 120.' Rows would then print as '4974 p2 1964-02 "Feb"' instead of '4974 p2 Y?2-02 "Feb"', and --raw would carry the NOTE above 'RAW LINES:'. printings --table AY-1 --row 1964-02 would then also resolve in the June 1970 issue.

notes: (1) show_table --raw prints only the header context and RAW LINES (otables.py ~1900-1906): no NOTES, no panel unstacking, no SIBLINGS hint. b used --raw for every table view and so never saw the tool's own analysis of the stacked layout; whatever v10 adds to NOTES must also be printed in --raw mode. (2) The tool already knows the structure ('4 column groups share the period stub (labels repeat every 3 columns); each group is a different run of years - unstacked below as panels 1..4', a[12]) and already lists siblings; it stops one step short of anchoring the years. When the header does carry the years (1970_05 sibling, c[37]) it fills every row's period correctly, so the anchoring code path exists. (3) printings' period inference on the 1965_12 'Trust Receipts' table ran the year backwards after the stub sequence 'YYYY-November, December, YYYY-January, February, ...' (a[108]-[110]): rows got periods 1965-01, 1964-02, 1963-03, ... and the SUMMARY presented one of them as the latest printing of the asked month. Both a and c caught it manually; b never got there. (4) All three cells assumed the pinned June 1970 issue must also hold the receipts and searched it for 20-50 steps; that issue prints only FY1969-70 monthly receipts. (5) The competing_candidates rule is inert-to-harmful: it restated b's own --alt as an 'Offer' and AGENTS.md told b the harness had computed it; b accepted without a reason. (6) c's detail-table value is within 1pct of the graded answer (one-decimal vs integer millions); a 'more precise' per-account table is a trap on this question, so v10 text should say precision is not a tie-breaker. (7) Cell a's own save (averages of each panel-year vs the annual series, a[99]-[100]) is a reusable consistency check the tool could run itself when anchoring: sibling match first, annual-average match as fallback.
